bindings.note: Panel backlight follows the CONSOLE knob on the light control panel.
Held at full. SL gates indices 4-17 entirely, so tying it to a cockpit dimmer would blank every lamp in daylight. Same reasoning as the Hornet profile.

Flag lamp brightness: NOSE, LEFT, RIGHT, FLAPS, HALF, FULL and HOOK. Follows the console dimmer at night, and goes full bright when the console is off, because console off means daylight and a dim flag lamp is unreadable then. The daylight case is the off value: a scale of a zero source resolves to zero, and a binding that resolves to zero takes its off value.
Gear handle warning light (red). Lit on gear disagreement or unsafe configuration, not on gear down.
Master Caution (yellow).
Nose gear safe (green).
Left gear safe (green).
Right gear safe (green).

Lit whenever the flaps are off the stops, so it covers travel as well as the settled positions. Measured 2026-09-16 with FLAPS_SWITCH captured alongside: retracted does NOT rest at zero. It undershoots to 34, rebounds to 462 and settles near 138, and a second capture settled at 0, so rest is somewhere in 0 to 462. The retracted rebound at 462 is higher than the first sample of real travel at 283, so those regions overlap and no floor separates them perfectly. 1000 clears the rebound with margin and costs about 50 ms of lateness at the start of extension, which is invisible. An earlier floor of 100 came from a capture that happened to reach exactly 0 and would have left this lamp lit with the flaps fully up.

Flaps arrived at DN. Measured 2026-09-16: DN settles at 65535 and rings down to 65206 before it stops, so 64000 clears the ringing. No lever condition is needed: DN is the top of travel, so nothing passes through this range on the way somewhere else. That simplification also kept this binding correct when the lever mapping turned out to be the reverse of what was inferred. Reading position rather than the lever also means an emergency retract shows the truth.

Lever at MVR and the flaps arrived there. FLAPS_SWITCH is MEASURED 2026-09-16: 0 = UP, 1 = MVR, 2 = DN. Note that is the reverse of what the DCS-BIOS description order 'DN - MVR - UP' suggests, so do not re-derive it from the definition. MVR settles at 22726 arriving from retracted and 23411 arriving from DN, ringing out to 22415 and 23476 across two captures. The window is deliberately wide enough for both directions and the overshoot. The lever condition is what stops HALF flashing when travelling straight from UP to DN, since the flaps pass through this window on the way.
Left engine fire (yellow). The jettison row reads left to right, so the fire warnings sit on it naturally.
APU fire (yellow), centre of the fire group.
Right engine fire (yellow).
UNDECIDED. Suggested: CANOPY_UNLOCKED (green).
UNDECIDED. Suggested: NOSEWHEEL_STEERING (green).
UNDECIDED. Suggested: GUN_READY, but that conflicts with the throttle A/G suggestion. GUN_READY can only go one place.
UNDECIDED. This is the physically dim lamp, so it should carry something that never needs catching at a glance. Suggested: MARKER_BEACON or TAKE_OFF_TRIM.
Throttle backlight follows the CONSOLE knob. Unlike the PTO2 SL, this only dims A/A and A/G, it does not gate them.
UNDECIDED. The A-10 has no master modes. Suggested: CMSC_LAUNCH (missile launch, red), which is worth having where your hand already is.
UNDECIDED. Suggested: GUN_READY, if it does not go to JETT instead.
